 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of their son Kurshid Alam S/o Nazrul Islam in a Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 13.12.2022 at about 4.42 a.m., when the son of the Petitioners by name Kurshid Alam was waiting for crossing the road near Hebbal signal, Hebbal circle,
Bengaluru, at that time, one Tata Intra bearing Reg.No.KA53AA6630 which was driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and when it was trying to overtake another lorry, it dashed against the Kurshid Alam.
Due to the impact, Kurshid Alam was fell down and sustained grievous head and body injuries and immediately he was taken to Baptist hospital, but, he was succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.
Thereafter, Postmortem was conducted at MS Ramaiah Hospital and then body was handed over to the Petitioners.
Petitioners had spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
3. Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.200/2023 healthy and he was working as a Security guard and was earning of Rs.20,000/ p.m.
The Petitioners entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Kurshid Alam, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Tata Intra bearing Reg.No.KA53AA 6630.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
4. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondents had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.1 filed its Objection statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further it contended that this accident took place solely due to Nazrul Islam vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30544660/
2 the carelessness and negligence of the deceased only.

sentences.text: Further it SCCH 15 5 MVC No.200/2023 contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Kurshid Alam S/o Nazrul Islam was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.12.2022 at about 4.42 a.m., on Hebbal Signal, near Hebbal circle, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Intra bearing Reg.No.KA53 AA6630 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Kurshid Alam?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.200/2023 3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to 10 and also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.P11 to 16 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.1 got examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 5 documents at Ex.R1 to 5 and closed its side evidence.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence.

7. Having heard arguments by both the sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative SCCH 15 7 MVC No.200/2023 Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".

14. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
15.
It is averred in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is SCCH 15 11 MVC No.200/2023 the father of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased Kurshid Alam.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of Petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.8 to 10 respectively.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased Kurshid Alam with the Petitioners.
Hence, the Petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Kurshid Alam.
16. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 22 years and he was working as a Security Guard at Private Eye Private Ltd. and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard PW.1 has examined one witness by name Tilakan, Regional Manager and he got marked 6 documents i.e., Pay slips with 65B Certificate and Service Record at Ex.P11 to 16.
PW.2 has deposed that the deceased Kurshid Alam was appointed as Security Guard in their company.
He admitted the suggestion that the actual salary of the deceased was Rs.17,446/.

Upon going through the Payslip i.e., Ex.P12 - the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.200/2023 Pay slip immediately previous month of the accident shows the basic salary is Rs.12,844/ and DA at Rs.4,602/ totally Rs.17,446/.
Hence, if the Professional Tax of Rs.200/ is deducted, then the salary of the deceased would be Rs.17,246/.
Hence, the same is to be taken for consideration.
17. Further, the Petitioner has stated the age of the deceased Kurshid Alam was 22 years at the time of the accident.
In this regard Petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P.10.
The date of birth of the deceased was shown as 25.02.2000.
The accident took place on 13.12.2022.
Hence, the age of the deceased Kurshid Alam was to be taken at 22 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :

19. The deceased has left behind his mother and father.
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees Nazrul Islam vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30544660/

wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held:

Yes:
there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork :
 executing Court directed to respondent  compute entitlement of claimants by  SCCH 15 17 MVC No.200/2023  adding 40 per cent of income for future  prospect and make corresponding deduction  towards personal expenses".

24. The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case person is selfemployed or fixed salary the addition should be 40% below the age of 40 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 22 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.17,246/ comes to Rs.6,898/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.24,144/ p.m. (Rs.17,246/ + Rs.6,898/ = Rs.24,144/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 18.

26.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Tata Intra bearing Reg.No.KA53AA6630.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

27. The Respondent No.1 has taken contention that on the alleged date of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess driving license and therefore it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

The Chargesheet which got marked by the PW.1 at Ex.P5 and the Chargesheet which got marked by the RW.1 at Ex.R2 shows that after thorough SCCH 15 20 MVC No.200/2023 investigation the I.O has submitted Chargesheet against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.3(1), 5(1), 181, 180 of IMV Act along with Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
28.

The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied on the Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.4716/2011(MV) in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt.
Umamaheshwari @ Umadevi and others and MFA No.6154/2019 (MVD) in between Hemalatha @

sentences.text: I have gone through the said decisions.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to discussed regarding liability, when the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the driving license and it has pleased to observed in the said Judgment

that the Respondent No.2  the owner of the vehicle neither contested the petition by filing Written SCCH 15 21 MVC No.200/2023 Statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that he did not consciously permit the driver of the vehicle to ride the vehicle
. Further, it observed that the rider of the vehicle without driving license was not impeached by him.

Hence, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the Respondent No.2 permitted operating of the vehicle by an unauthorized person and the said act of Respondent No.2 amounts to fundamental breach of policy condition within the meaning of Sec.149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition.
Accordingly, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to partly allowed the appeal and confirmed the dismissal of the claim petition against the Respondent No.1.

sentences.text: In the instant case also the Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle appeared before the Court through his Counsel, but, he did not choose to contest the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.200/2023 matter by filing the Written Statement nor adduce any evidence claiming that he did not consciously permit the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the offending vehicle.
Further the Charge sheet clearly shows that the driver of the offending vehicle was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.

Moreover,
the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., the Respondent No.2 has been Chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.5(1) and 180 of IMV Act for permitting the person who did not possess driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.

Therefore, this tribunal is also of the opinion that the above said Judgments of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka is aptly applicable to the case in hand and the Respondent No.2 being the owner of the vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "in the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.200/2023 Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,32,552/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents No.2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,32,552/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.200/2023 Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay  the compensation amount to the  Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% each to the Petitioner No.1 and 2.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Nazrul Islam vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30544660/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,07,552/ towards loss of dependency.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
27. The Respondent No.1 has taken contention that on the alleged date of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess driving license and therefore it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Chargesheet which got marked by the PW.1 at Ex.P5 and the Chargesheet which got marked by the RW.1 at Ex.R2 shows that after thorough SCCH 15 20 MVC No.200/2023 investigation the I.O has submitted Chargesheet against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.3(1), 5(1), 181, 180 of IMV Act along with Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
28.
Hence, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the Respondent No.2 permitted operating of the vehicle by an unauthorized person and the said act of Respondent No.2 amounts to fundamental breach of policy condition within the meaning of Sec.149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition.
Accordingly, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to partly allowed the appeal and confirmed the dismissal of the claim petition against the Respondent No.1.
Nazrul Islam vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30544660/
8 30.
In the instant case also the Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle appeared before the Court through his Counsel, but, he did not choose to contest the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.200/2023 matter by filing the Written Statement nor adduce any evidence claiming that he did not consciously permit the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the offending vehicle.
Further the Charge sheet clearly shows that the driver of the offending vehicle was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
Moreover,
the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., the Respondent No.2 has been Chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.5(1) and 180 of IMV Act for permitting the person who did not possess driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
